authors: Claude Code session (holant lead, step b)

links.note: Exact rank computation replacing the row's planned bias check. Rank over F_p is an exact computation; the comparison across multiplier families is descriptive except for the preregistered full-rank rule.

question: For random multipliers b_i, does the evaluation matrix of degree-<=D monomials in the coordinates of ([b_1]R, ..., [b_t]R), over all candidate logs, reach full rank once the monomial count is about twice the number of candidates (p from 2^8 to 2^11)?

claims.text: Random-multiplier evaluation matrices reach full rank at monomial/candidate ratio about 2 on at least 90% of cells at every size (the interpolation attack's condition holds at toy size), by the preregistered rule.
claims.if_supported: H1 of the low-degree lead is refuted at toy size with an explicit query-cheap attack; the row restates to H1' (proved)
claims.if_not_supported: a structural rank deficit for elliptic multiples, worth a note; H1 survives this test

hypotheses.statement: Full rank at ratio about 2 for random multipliers (heuristic of the desk note).
hypotheses.mechanism: for random large b_i, the points ([b_i]R) behave like generic points for low-degree polynomials beyond the t curve equations

data_seen.measured: full rank at p=101 (t=4, D=3); 161/222 at p=211 for the same (t,D), ratio < 1

arms.description: random multipliers b_i in [2, N-2], a_i = 0
uniformly random points of F_p^{2t} in place of the curve points

aa.not_applicable_reason: ranks are exact deterministic computations; there is no measurement noise for an A/A arm to calibrate, and replicate-to-replicate variation within the rand arm is itself reported

positive.expected_detection: rank <= 3Dt+1 < candidates: the detector reports a deficit where one is proved

null_population.description: uniformly random point sets of the same size in F_p^{2t}
null_population.why_n: 3 replicates x 37 instances; checks that generic points give full rank min(C, #monomials)

factors.name: size
factors.value: p = largest prime below 2^L, L in 8,9,10 (full grid) and 11 (one decisive instance)

factors.name: curve
factors.how: 2 curves per size (1 at L=11), prime order != p, distinct orders, seeded by derive_seed(sha,'curve',L,0)

factors.name: t
factors.value: t chosen so C(2t+D,D)/(N-1) is nearest to 0.5, 1, 2 on a log scale

factors.name: generator
factors.value: first point with y != 0 found by scanning x

randomization.arm_order_reason: exact deterministic computations; order cannot change a rank

seed_derivation.note: tools/experiment_protocol.py derive_seed(protocol_sha, arm, instance index, replicate) for every row; curves by derive_seed(sha,'curve',L,0)

instance_sampling.rule: instances fixed by instances(); curves drawn before any rank is computed

blinding.how: frozen script applies a fixed rule

power.note: ranks are exact; the rule is a threshold on full-rank fractions over 12 to 18 decisive cells per size (3 at L=11), not a significance test

preflight_runtime.measured_on: this container; 1998x3654 at p=2039: build 0.4 s, rank 80 s (rank not read); 1020x2040 random 7 s

primary.name: full-rank fraction, random multipliers, ratio >= 1.5
primary.definition: fraction of rand (instance, replicate) cells with monomials/candidates >= 1.5 whose rank equals the candidate count, per size
primary.formula: mean(full) over decisive cells, per L

secondary.name: rank deficit against the generic expectation
secondary.definition: expected_generic - rank, expected_generic = min(C, #monomials - t*C(2t+D-3, D-3)) (D < 6) or min(C,#monomials) for null

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design: 37 instances x 4 arms x 3 replicates = 444 matrices, then stop

decision_rule.text: Validity: null full (rank == min(C,#monomials)) in >= 95% of null cells, and every shift cell rank <= 3Dt+1, else INVALID_CONTROLS. HOLDS iff the full-rank fraction of rand cells with ratio >= 1.5 is >= 0.9 at every size. FAILS iff that fraction is <= 0.5 at L = 10 and L = 11. Otherwise MIXED.

inadmissible: changing sizes, (t, D) rule, curves, multipliers or the decision rule after seeing ranks
reading HOLDS as a practical attack: the attack's local work is about N^omega field operations
